name: SambaNova SN40L Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU)
memory_type: three-tier: 520 MiB on-chip PMU SRAM, 64 GiB co-packaged HBM, up to 1.5 TiB DDR DRAM
memory_bandwidth_basis: NULL, AND HERE IS WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR (2026-10-11). arXiv:2405.07518 reports 520 MiB on-chip PMU SRAM providing hundreds of TB/s on-chip memory bandwidth, 64 GiB co-packaged HBM (per-socket GB/s not stated as a discrete number), and DDR DRAM tier with peak bandwidth over 200 GB/s, with DDR-to-HBM model loading over 1 TB/s across an 8-socket SN40L node. Per-chip HBM bandwidth in GB/s is not published directly by the vendor in the whitepaper.

onchip_cache.source_note: arXiv:2405.07518: 520 MiB of on-chip PMU (Pattern Memory Unit) SRAM per SN40L RDU socket distributed across 1040 PMUs.

flops.basis_detail: arXiv:2405.07518, Section 1: Each SN40L RDU socket has 638 BF16 TFLOPS of peak compute performance using 1040 distributed Pattern Compute Units (PCUs).

notes: SambaNova SN40L is fabricated on TSMC 5nm using 2.5D Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS) packaging containing two SN40L Reconfigurable Dataflow Dies (RDDs) and co-packaged HBM. It features a unique three-tier memory hierarchy: 520 MiB on-chip PMU SRAM, 64 GiB on-package HBM, and up to 1.5 TiB of directly attached DDR DRAM (via pluggable DIMMs). Peak compute is 638 BF16 TFLOPS per socket across 1040 PCUs. TDP is not published at the individual socket level (16-socket rack is air-cooled in standard 19-inch form factor delivering 10.2 BF16 PFLOPS aggregate roofline). All numbers transcribed directly from SambaNova technical paper (arXiv:2405.07518) and blog post.
